description_en: A stone fountain from approximately 13th-15th century.The monument is found in the northern part of the Bhurtī Temple Complex. The site itself is located in the northern end of the settlement of Bhurtī, 3 km north of Narayana, the district headquarters. It currently comprises 22 standingśikharatemples (ordevala) and one stone fountain. Architectural activity at the site can be situated between the 13thand 15thcentury, a time period corresponding to the latter part of the Khaśa Malla empire and the early phase of the Rāskoṭi dynasty (Andolfatto 2019,Pokharel 2011: 128-129,Sharma 1972: 23-31,Sharma 2012: 120-123).In 2008, the “Bhurti Temple Complex of Dailekh” was enlisted on UNESCO’s World Heritage Tentative List by the Government of Nepal (criteriaiiandiv).The fountain is oriented towards the west. It is constituted of a central panel carved with pilasters and a horizontal frieze ofāmalakamotifs. Water used to be delivered through two stylised makara heads. A small plaftorm is placed on each side of the central panel. Similar fountains, locally referred to asmugrāhā, are found throughout the region (Andolfatto 2019: 101-102). Given the estimate period of architectural activity at the site, it is possible to suggest that this fountain was built between the 13th and 15th century.Dhārā, is a term of Sanskrit origin often used in western Nepal for fountains. Another term, vernacular, ismugrāhā.
monument_assessment: Slightly damaged (minor damages such as minor cracks, plants, missing stones in plinths)
